concept: Replica set oplog window and initial sync
summary: Source-anchored research for Replica set oplog window and initial sync. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Initial sync adds traffic and load to its source. Schedule resynchronization when bandwidth and workload permit; cloning includes index construction, so index footprint forms part of initial-sync work. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/resync-replica-set-member.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md

Kevin Adistambha's October 2020 forum explanation dates concurrent oplog tailing during the clone phase to MongoDB 3.4. Current documentation and implementation descriptions support the buffering mechanism, so pre-3.4 whole-copy-window guidance needs historical qualification. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/more-info-on-mongodb-initial-sync-architecture/9727/4 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md

The oplog window measures retained history in time. If all eligible sync sources have overwritten entries a secondary still needs, ordinary replication cannot catch up and a full resynchronization is required. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-oplog.md ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/resync-replica-set-member.md

If a secondary's required replication position predates the oldest oplog entry on every eligible sync source, ordinary oplog replication cannot catch it up. MongoDB's replication implementation describes rejecting a sync source whose oldest oplog entry is newer than the node's newest entry because it is too far ahead, and waiting for manual intervention (likely a resync) when the secondary is too far behind all candidates. A Percona article says the same: a node too far behind the eligible sync source enters maintenance and resync must be called manually. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-replica-set-scenarios-and-internals/

Oplog size is not the only requirement for initial-sync success. During steps 3 and 4 the syncing node checks continuity of operations against the source, and a gap restarts the initial sync. A persistent network error also restarts the initial sync from the beginning. The target needs enough disk space in the local database to hold the buffered oplog records. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md

For collection-buffered logical initial sync, the whole initial sync need not fit in one source oplog window. Oplog entries are pulled and buffered during the copy, and the manual requires an oplog window covering steps 3 and 4, where a continuity gap restarts the sync. The manual's Oplog Window section also says the window must be long enough to fetch entries between the start and end of the logical initial sync. Provision disk space in the target's local database for the buffer. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/more-info-on-mongodb-initial-sync-architecture/9727/4

The oplog window measures retained history in time, rather than merely the configured oplog capacity in bytes. Percona's monitoring documentation defines Oplog Range as the total time span covered by the oplog from oldest to newest entry. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html

Logical initial sync clones all databases except local, builds collection indexes in parallel with the data clone, and then applies oplog records buffered during the copy and the remaining oplog changes. MongoDB's manual describes these as distinct stages. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md

Logical initial sync fetches oplog entries during data cloning and buffers them in a destination-side collection for later application. The destination needs disk space for this buffer in local; sizing only the source oplog omits a separate storage requirement. (high confidence)

The source oplog window should cover expected maintenance and downtime, and the time needed to restore a member from backup. Snapshot seed files must be recent enough for the restored member to catch up using retained oplog entries. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-checklist-operations.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/resync-replica-set-member.md

Percona PMM distinguishes oldest-to-newest Oplog Range from current-time-to-oldest Now to End, and exposes oplog generation in GB/hour. These metrics help assess retention as workload changes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

AceMQ reports that nightly ETL bursts repeatedly pushed secondaries beyond retained oplog history, causing full initial syncs that competed with subsequent loads. It reports eliminating recurring nightly resyncs through oplog resizing, reduced write amplification, and staggered concurrency. This is an anonymous customer case without published raw measurements, not a general performance guarantee. (low confidence)

As an operational inference, size the oplog on retained time under peak oplog generation, with headroom for disruption. Percona's PMM dashboard shows both the oplog recovery window and oplog GB/hour, and advises increasing the oplog size when retention is shorter than the backup window. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html
